conventions.deferred:: A real obligation this plan carries; the suffix names the milestone whose scope in PLAN.md the clause falls in — S6, the transaction layer's. The note names the gap that keeps the clause out of the carrier set. An entry with this value says that nothing under lean/ or vectors/ carries the clause's requirement: a missing carrier is recorded rather than covered by naming a declaration that does not hold the rule.
conventions.formalized:: A Lean declaration path that carries this clause's meaning. Every path recorded here names a declaration the module it names actually holds, and the ledger's existence gate resolves it against lean/** rather than taking the note's word for it; where the carrier is the *condition* a refusal carries rather than the frame that would carry it, the note says which half is missing.
conventions.kind: The clause's own keyword, read from the ledger's clause rather than inferred from the coverage class: the class is MUST for both forms, so kind and class diverge for MUST NOT, and one clause here is a MUST NOT.
conventions.test:: A vector id whose verdict is the clause's observable form; the ledger's vector gate resolves every id recorded here against vectors/**.

design_consequences: These two clauses are the `global-id` pair the transaction layer's machine turns on: the capability rule is carried and pinned by a positive and a negative vector, and the association between the allocated txn-id and the global id is not modelled at all — the field is read for its presence rather than its value.

Together with the error-path clauses of this file, the read is: what the machine decides with the fields it holds is carried; what would need a quantity it does not hold — a global id, a source's capabilities, a frame to send — is deferred with that gap named.

One correction inside this file: `txn-declare.5` was first recorded as carried by the layer's refusal vocabulary, and it is not — the vocabulary is real but the *declare* path raises no transaction-error, so the clause is deferred with the vocabulary named as the near-miss. The distinction is the one the whole pass rests on: a declaration that recognises a clause's vocabulary does not carry its rule.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: Specifies that the txn-id allocated by this declare MUST be associated with the indicated global transaction.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: Blocked: lean/Spec/Transactions.lean line 324 def declare; :326 refuseUnless (!settled); :332-334 the globalId capability guard

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: This field MUST NOT be set if the coordinator does not have the «distributed-transactions» capability.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: A declare carrying `global-id` is refused when the coordinator's announced capabilities do not include `distributed-transactions`: `declare`'s second guard reads the coordinator's capabilities for the direction the declare travels and refuses with the `amqp-error` family's `invalid-field` as class `malformed` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:286-300), and `Contracts.Transaction.DeclareGlobalIdRefused` states it as a proposition over the same function. Both vectors cite the clause: the refused declare, and the admitted one that contrasts with it by announcing the capability.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: This message MUST NOT be sent settled as the sender is REQUIRED to receive and interpret the outcome of the declare from the receiver.
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: A settled declare is refused, whichever end sends it: `declare`'s first guard is `refuseUnless (!settled)` with the artifact's own reason, that the sender is required to receive and interpret the outcome (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:286-296). The contract states it as a proposition over the same function (`Contracts.Transaction.DeclareSettledRefused`), and three vectors cite the clause — two of them the settled declare and the settled discharge, the third the conforming exchange that contrasts with them.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If the coordinator was unable to perform the «declare» as specified by the transaction controller, the transaction coordinator MUST convey the error to the controller as a «transaction-error».
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: lean/Contracts/Transaction.lean line 37-39 ('Disposition outcomes are the link layer's ... the frames that carry it ... belong to the link layer'); lean/Spec/Transactions.lean line 326-334 declare's only refusals carry illegal-state and malformed, never a transaction-error

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If the «source» for the link to the «coordinator» supports the «rejected» outcome, then the message MUST be «rejected» with this outcome carrying the «transaction-error».
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: lean/Contracts/Transaction.lean line 37-39; lean/Spec/Transactions.lean line 300-317 coordinatorCapabilities reads only the coordinator target's announced capabilities, never a source's

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If the «source» does not support the «rejected» outcome, the transactional resource MUST «detach» the link to the coordinator, with the «detach» performative carrying the «transaction-error».
If the coordinator is unable to complete the «discharge», the coordinator MUST convey the error to the controller as a «transaction-error».
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: The discharge's own error path is carried and exercised: a discharge naming an id this endpoint does not hold live is refused with the `transaction-error` family's `unknown-id` (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:313-324, with the condition read from the table at :150-160), and two vectors cite the clause — the unknown id and the second discharge of the same id. What is not built is the frame the condition would travel in, as `.txn-declare.5` records.

amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.clause_text: If the «source» for the link to the «coordinator» supports the «rejected» outcome, then the message MUST be «rejected» with this outcome carrying the «transaction-error».
If the «source» does not support the «rejected» outcome, the transactional resource MUST «detach» the link to the coordinator, with the «detach» performative carrying the «transaction-error».
Note that the coordinator MUST always be able to complete a «discharge» where the fail flag is set to true (since coordinator failure leads to rollback, which is what the controller is asking for).
amqp-core-transactions-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:.note: A `fail=true` discharge completes whatever the register holds, and the machine implements it by retiring the id *before* consulting liveness (lean/Spec/Transactions.lean:313-324) — the branch the artifact's 'always able to complete' is about. `Contracts.Transaction.FailDischargeCompletes` states it as a law over the same function, the vector cites the clause, and the interaction the sentence provokes — a `fail=true` discharge naming an id that was never allocated — is decided in the register at `ledger/ambiguities/fail-true-against-an-unknown-id.json`.
